industries.rationale: The bill directly affects the regulatory process banks must follow when seeking approval to merge with other banks.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a September 2024 rule from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that changed how bank merger applications are reviewed. If this resolution passes, those procedural changes would be nullified and the prior review process would remain in effect.

bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-10.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects overdraft fee revenue and regulatory compliance obligations at very large financial institutions.

If enacted, the resolution would prevent the rule from taking effect, leaving existing overdraft fee practices in place.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: MORE USDA Grants Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill expands access to USDA rural development grants that support farming communities and agribusiness infrastructure in qualifying counties.
The bill specifically includes Distance Learning and Telemedicine Grants, which fund broadband and telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas.
Community Facilities grants often fund construction of public buildings and infrastructure, creating demand for contractors in eligible counties.

bill.plainSummary: This bill makes it easier for local and tribal governments in rural counties where the federal government owns more than half the land to access certain USDA grant programs. It cuts their required matching funds in half, gives them priority if they haven't received grants in the past decade, and directs USDA to provide extra technical help and flexibility during the application process. The grants cover rural business development, community facilities, telemedicine, and other rural development programs.

bill.title: Stop Russian Market Manipulation Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: The bill directly restricts imports of eight specific metals and minerals, affecting companies that source, process, or trade these materials.
Manufacturers that rely on platinum-group metals, nickel, copper, or zinc as inputs would face supply-chain changes and potentially higher costs.
Defense contractors use platinum-group metals and specialty alloys in aerospace and weapons systems, making supply sourcing relevant.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would ban the import of eight minerals—platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium, nickel, copper, zinc, and braggite—if they are produced in Russia or by Russian entities. The ban would also cover minerals obtained through swaps or other arrangements designed to evade the restriction. The prohibition would remain in effect until one year after the President certifies that Russia has ended hostilities against Ukraine, and would resume if Russia restarts hostilities within three years.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending information about veterans or their beneficiaries to the national firearm background-check database solely because they have someone appointed to manage their benefits. The VA could still share such information if a court has found the person to be a danger to themselves or others.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns. Veterans and their families.

bill.title: Small County PILT Parity Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 474.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects federal payments to county and local governments that host tax-exempt federal lands.
Counties with significant federal land often host mining operations on those lands, and changes to local revenue formulas may indirectly affect permitting and local fiscal capacity.
Federal lands in small counties frequently include oil, gas, or coal extraction sites, and local revenue changes may affect the fiscal environment for these operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would modify federal payments to local governments that contain tax-exempt federal land. Specifically, it appears to adjust the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) formula for small counties, which compensates localities for property-tax revenue they cannot collect on federally owned land. Without access to the bill text, the precise nature of the change to the formula or eligibility criteria cannot be described.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who pays federal tax.

bill.title: Pregnant Students’ Rights Act
bill.latestActionText: Cloture on the motion to proceed to the measure not invoked in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 45. Record Vote Number: 12. (CR S286)

industries.rationale: The bill imposes new disclosure and information requirements on institutions of higher education participating in federal student aid programs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require colleges and universities that receive federal student aid to provide information to students about resources and accommodations available for carrying a pregnancy to term and caring for a baby after birth. Schools would need to list both on-campus and community resources, explain available accommodations for pregnant and parenting students, and provide information on how to file discrimination complaints related to a student's decision to continue a pregnancy.

plain.whoItTouches: College students, and their families.

bill.title: Firearm Access During Shutdowns Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects firearm manufacturers and dealers by ensuring background checks and export licenses continue to be processed during shutdowns.
The bill changes staffing and operational requirements for FBI, ATF, Commerce, and State Department employees during government shutdowns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires certain federal firearms-related operations to continue during government shutdowns. It designates background-check processing by the FBI, enforcement activities by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and firearm export-license processing by the Commerce and State Departments as essential services. Employees performing these functions would be classified as excepted workers who must report during a shutdown.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.
